references.text: Protoevangelium – the first messianic prophecy in the Books of Moses: the woman's offspring shall crush the serpent's head. Jesus explained from Moses how the Scriptures testified about him ([ref:1 Mos 3:15|Genesis 3:15]).
The promise to Abraham that in his offspring all the families of the earth shall be blessed – a fundamental messianic prophecy from the Books of Moses ([ref:1 Mos 22:18|Genesis 22:18]).
Jacob's prophecy that the scepter shall not depart from Judah – a messianic text from the Books of Moses which Jesus may have explained to his disciples ([ref:1 Mos 49:10|Genesis 49:10]).
The bronze serpent lifted up in the wilderness is a type of Christ (cf. [ref:Joh 3:14|John 3:14]), a text from Moses pointing to Jesus' crucifixion ([ref:4 Mos 21:9|Numbers 21:9]).
Moses' prophecy about a prophet like himself whom the Lord shall raise up – a central messianic text from the Books of Moses ([ref:5 Mos 18:15-18|Deuteronomy 18:15-18]).
Psalm 22 describes the suffering Messiah with details of the crucifixion: pierced hands and feet, casting lots for his garments. A prophetic text about Christ ([ref:Sal 22:1-31|Psalm 22:1-31]).
David's psalm about the Messiah as Lord and priest forever in the order of Melchizedek – a central prophetic text that Jesus himself referred to ([ref:Sal 110:1-4|Psalm 110:1-4]).
Isaiah's prophecy about the virgin who shall conceive and bear a son, Immanuel – a prophecy about Christ ([ref:Jes 7:14|Isaiah 7:14]).

The Lord's suffering servant who bears our sickness and sorrow, pierced for our transgressions – one of the most important prophetic passages concerning Christ's suffering and death ([ref:Jes 53:1-12|Isaiah 53:1-12]).
Daniel's prophecy about the seventy weeks and the anointed one who shall be cut off – a time-specific messianic prophecy ([ref:Dan 9:24-26|Daniel 9:24-26]).
Micah's prophecy about the ruler who shall come forth from Bethlehem – a prophecy concerning the birthplace of the Messiah ([ref:Mi 5:2|Micah 5:2]).
Zechariah's prophecy about him whom they have pierced – a prophecy concerning Christ's crucifixion ([ref:Sak 12:10|Zechariah 12:10]).
Later in the same chapter, Jesus repeats the same point: everything written about him in the Law of Moses, the Prophets and the Psalms must be fulfilled ([ref:Luk 24:44|Luke 24:44]).
Philip testifies to Nathanael: "He whom Moses wrote about in the Law, and whom the prophets wrote about, him we have found" – the same principle as in Luke 24:27 ([ref:Joh 1:45|John 1:45]).
Jesus says: "You search the Scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life – and it is they that bear witness about me" ([ref:Joh 5:39|John 5:39]).
Jesus says that Moses wrote about him: "For if you believed Moses, you would believe me. For it is about me he has written" ([ref:Joh 5:46-47|John 5:46-47]).
Peter's speech where he quotes Moses' prophecy about the prophet who is to come, and states that all the prophets from Samuel onward have proclaimed these days ([ref:Apg 3:22-24|Acts 3:22-24]).
Philip began with the Scripture (Isaiah 53) and preached the gospel of Jesus to the Ethiopian eunuch – a direct parallel to Jesus' approach in Luke 24:27 ([ref:Apg 8:35|Acts 8:35]).
Peter testifies that all the prophets testify about Jesus: "To him all the prophets bear witness" ([ref:Apg 10:43|Acts 10:43]).
Paul testifies that he says nothing other than what the prophets and Moses said would happen: that the Christ should suffer and as the first rise from the dead ([ref:Apg 26:22-23|Acts 26:22-23]).

Peter writes that the prophets searched and examined the salvation they prophesied about – they did not serve themselves, but us, with the message of Christ's sufferings and glory ([ref:1 Pet 1:10-12|1 Peter 1:10-12]).
